messages:
support_jamie: FYI — got 3 customer p99/95 complaints from eu-west around 10:45 UTC. All started after last night's CUDA15 + driver push. Alerts show hostfs qdepth spike and KV cache miss storm.

emma_oncall: ack, I'm pulling up graphs. Which customers and pods?

ben_infra: I see the same on host node eu-west-2a-03 — device avg queue depth jumped from ~4 to 48, throughput steady. Link: https://grafana.redwood/host/eu-west-2a-03 (will paste charts) :eyes:

raj_runtime: Are these hosted-api customers or Dedicated? Any tenant-config differences (kv-cache enabled, io cgroups)?

support_jamie: hosted customers primarily, medium q (many short chat requests). KV cache is enabled by default for these routes. sample trace IDs: trace-9a7b, trace-c3d2. Attached log snippet:```kernel: nvme0: I/O 0 Q(0) timeout, reset controller
nvme0n1: I/O 9845 queued for 120s```

monitoring_bot: Alert: hostfs_qdepth > 30 (eu-west-2a-03) 10:43:21 UTC — anomaly 12x above baseline

emma_oncall: Repro steps requested: can someone run fio on a repro VM with same OS/driver? Need to confirm host vs driver regression. In meantime, try isolating one noisy tenant.

ben_infra: Quick mitigation I can roll out: (1) throttle IO for noisy pods with blkio cgroup (io.max) to cap bandwidth, (2) move some routes to fallback pool with older driver nodes. Command to limit: ```echo "8:0 rbps=10485760 wbps=5242880" > /sys/fs/cgroup/io.slice/io.max``` — will stage to 1 pod first.

alice_cs: Customers want ETA and mitigation now — any chance we can do routing fallback at the API layer to route critical traffic to eu-west-1 where rollout hasn't happened?

raj_runtime: Yes — we can add a temporary routing rule to prefer eu-west-1 for specific tenant IDs and low-latency routes. That buys time for infra rollback. I'll open a canary routing flag.

support_jamie: also seeing increased tokenization latency in logs — suspect KV cache churn due to backend IO stalls. If KV writes slow, cache misses spike and requests amplify IO.

emma_oncall: Good catch. Mitigation idea: disable KV prefetch/persist for affected tenants (turn cache to readonly) so we stop writes and reduce hostfs pressure. Can we flip that quickly?

ben_infra: I can push a config change to set kv_cache.mode=readonly for `tenant:acme-ads` and two others. Rolling it to 3 tenants now :thumbsup:

monitoring_bot: Event: kv_cache.mode set -> readonly for tenant acme-ads, rolled in 3 hosts (eu-west-2a).

emma_oncall: After readonly flip, qdepth dropped to ~12 in ~6m. p95 improved but p99 still elevated for some traces. We need a reproducible fio job and kernel dmesg collection.

raj_runtime: I'll coordinate a repro: create fio profile that mimics many small random sync writes + concurrent small reads to emulate KV workload. Share script:```fio --name=kv_sim --ioengine=libaio --rw=randrw --rwmixread=70 --bs=4k --numjobs=24 --size=4G --runtime=300 --iodepth=32```

ben_infra: Running that on a spare host with CUDA15 driver — reproduces qdepth spike and occasional nvme reset messages. Suspect driver/firmware scheduling regression interacting badly with host kernel IO scheduler.

alice_cs: Customers still in chat. Can we offer temporary SLA credits + routing to eu-west-1? I suggested that to PMs.

emma_oncall: Short-term plan: 1) Keep kv cache readonly for affected tenants, 2) Route critical customers to eu-west-1 fallback, 3) Throttle noisy pods with io.max, 4) Start driver bisect and contact vendor for kernel/driver interaction.

raj_runtime: For rollback path: we can roll nodes in pool back to driver vXXX (pre-CUDA15) using the existing image snapshot. Ben, can you validate the rollback image boots and canary?

ben_infra: Validating now — quick smoke shows older driver avoids the nvme reset under fio. If validated, I'll schedule a staged rollback for the affected AZ (eu-west-2a), canary 2 hosts then 6 hosts.

support_jamie: I'll send templated customer update now with mitigation steps and ETA.

emma_oncall: Logging follow-ups: collect /var/log/kern.log, dmesg, nvme-cli outputs, and oprofile traces from affected hosts; attach to incident ticket. Also tag vendor driver team with trace IDs.

raj_runtime: Adding test note: try switching kernel IO scheduler to mq-deadline on canary to see if scheduling change helps — we should test before full rollback.

ben_infra: Agreed. I'll test io scheduler + rollback in parallel to get faster signal.

alice_cs: Thanks team. Customer comms sent. :pray:

emma_oncall: Summary for incident ticket: root cause under investigation — likely regression introduced by CUDA15+driver interacting with NVMe driver/host IO scheduler causing KV cache write stalls -> qdepth surge -> p95/p99 regression. Mitigations applied: kv cache readonly, io cgroup throttles, routing fallback, canary rollback in progress. Next update in 30m.

monitoring_bot: Incident status: mitigations applied; p95 trending down, p99 partial improvement.

support_jamie: thx — keeping this thread updated with any customer replies.
